title: Smoke Test — Counter Check-in for an Awaiting-Payment Attendee
subtitle: Two outcomes at the door: pay the correct amount, vs. comp them. Same order (O-6FDWJZ5, $100), reset between scenarios.

meta.Flow: Public check-in door (unauthenticated link) → CheckInOptionsModal; contrasted with authenticated Manage-Order Payments panel
meta.Order: O-6FDWJZ5 (id 15), staged to AWAITING_OFFLINE_PAYMENT / $100, attendee Sam Spade (A-ZV8IDXP) AWAITING_PAYMENT
meta.Key design point: The door can take a correct full payment, but CANNOT comp — comping a receivable is gated behind the authenticated Manage-Order surface.
meta.Data: Order 15 staged + reset between scenarios; restored via ops/smoke/checkin-payment/RESTORE.sql

steps.title: Door — attendee is awaiting payment
steps.description: The check-in agent opens the public check-in list and finds Sam Spade flagged 'Awaiting payment' (VIP). Because the event allows awaiting-offline-payment check-ins, the row is actionable rather than blocked.

steps.title: Door modal — pay or check-in only, NO comp
steps.description: Tapping Check In opens the door options modal: an 'Unpaid Order' alert with exactly two choices — 'Check in only' and 'Check in and record payment'. There is deliberately no comp/write-off/arbitrary-amount option here: the door link is unauthenticated, and comping a receivable is a financial decision kept off it.
steps.notes: This is the central design boundary the two scenarios pivot on.

steps.title: Scenario A — they pay the correct amount
steps.description: 'Check in and record payment' expands to a payment-method picker (Cash) + optional reference. The agent records the full payment at the counter. The amount is never typed freehand — it settles the full balance via the ledger.

steps.title: Scenario A — checked in, order paid in full
steps.description: Submitting checks the attendee in and marks the order paid. The 'Awaiting payment' flag clears from the row.

steps.title: Scenario A — Manage-Order confirms settlement
steps.description: The authenticated Payments panel shows Owed $100.00 / Collected $100.00 / Settled, with a single CASH $100.00 ledger row ('Cash at door — paid in full'). The order's total_gross was never rewritten — the door payment is a typed credit against the balance.

steps.title: Scenario B — same order, reset to outstanding
steps.description: Order reset to awaiting payment ($100 outstanding, nothing collected). The authenticated Manage-Order Payments panel exposes the action the door cannot: 'Comp remaining $100.00' (alongside Record payment with arbitrary amount/method/donation).
steps.notes: Comp lives only here — an authenticated, role-gated surface.

steps.title: Scenario B — remainder comped
steps.description: Clicking Comp remaining writes a non-cash COMP $100.00 ledger row. The panel now reads Comped $100.00, Collected $0.00, Settled. No money was collected, but the balance is cleared.
steps.notes: Contrast with Scenario A: a COMP row (non-cash) vs. a CASH receipt. Collected stays $0.

steps.title: Scenario B — attendee now active at the door
steps.description: Back on the check-in list, Sam Spade no longer shows 'Awaiting payment'. Settling the balance (here via comp) flipped the attendee to ACTIVE, so the door now offers a plain check-in.

steps.title: Scenario B — direct check-in, no payment prompt
steps.description: Tapping Check In admits the attendee immediately ('Sam checked in successfully') — the unpaid-order modal does not appear, confirming the comp fully resolved the order at the counter.
